Subject: Data locality requirements — questions after discovery call

Hi Maya / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a short set of clarifying questions so we can map a proposal that meets your compliance needs. Marissa and Ben are copied to help with technical and commercial follow-ups; Aditya (Legal) is on standby for contract questions.

Recap (short):
- OrchardPay will process EU customer payments and associated PII; primary concern is EU data residency for EU-origin data, and strong controls for logs and backups.
- You are evaluating hosted vs dedicated/private deployment for production (stage 1: hosted pilot, stage 2: dedicated for EU).

Questions we promised to capture — please reply inline if helpful:
1) Data ingress/PII: Do you consider any request payload fields (payment method identifier, billing address) to be PII that must never leave the EU? Or can we tokenize before leaving region (i.e., store encrypted token centrally)?
2) Retention: What is your retention policy for (a) conversational inputs, (b) system logs/traces, and (c) model prompt caching? Please specify min/max (e.g., 90 / 365 / 0).
3) Logging controls: Must logs be redact-only (no payload), or may we store hashed fingerprints for debugging? Any required retention period for audit logs?
4) Data residency & failover: For EU customers you want pinning — do you require hard pin (no cross-region replication) or a primary-in-region with DR copies in another region encrypted and access-controlled? If DR copies are allowed, do they need to be encrypted with a customer-managed KMS?
5) Backups / snapshots: RPO/RTO expectations for production — are you expecting same-region point-in-time backups only or geo-replication for faster failover?
6) Compliance artifacts: Which of these would you want up front — SOC 2 Type II report, penetration test summary, encryption whitepaper, or a detailed dataflow diagram?

Next steps we propose from Redwood:
- We will draft a short residency options table (hosted EU pin, hosted EU with DR, dedicated EU, private on-prem) with cost delta and operational tradeoffs.
- Ben to propose a technical design for tokenization + KMS options for EU data flows.
- Schedule a 30m follow-up next week to confirm the MAP (mutual action plan) and any gating items for procurement.

Can you confirm the retention numbers and the preferred failover behavior? If you prefer, reply with the OrchardPay security matrix and we’ll annotate it.

Thanks —

Thanks, Karthik — great summary. Inline answers below; attaching our security matrix (OrchardPay_Security_Matrix.pdf).

1) Data ingress/PII: For EU customers, any raw payment identifiers, billing address, and national ID numbers are considered PII and must not leave the EU in raw form. Tokenization is acceptable, provided tokens cannot be reversed without keys we control.

2) Retention:
- conversational inputs: store up to 30 days for debugging, then purge (longer retention not allowed for EU-origin PII);
- system logs/traces: retain 365 days for audit (may be redacted for payloads);
- prompt caching: avoid caching raw prompts containing PII — hashed fingerprints are OK.

3) Logging controls: We require payload redaction for any PII in logs. Storing salted hashes/fingerprints for debug correlation is acceptable, but only for internal use and logged access must be audited.

4) Data residency & failover: Preferred: hard pin to EU for production traffic. For DR we can accept encrypted geo-replicated backups provided:
  - backups are encrypted with a KMS key managed by OrchardPay (customer-managed keys),
  - access to DR copies requires MFA + documented approval,
  - replication only used for DR exercises with clear notice and audit trail.

5) Backups / snapshots: RPO <= 4 hours, RTO target <= 2 hours for production. Same-region snapshots preferred; geo-replication allowed for DR with customer-managed keys (see above).

6) Compliance artifacts: Please share SOC 2 Type II, encryption whitepaper, and a dataflow diagram showing where tokens/KMS live. A pen-test summary would help but can come later.

We can make time for a 30m follow-up on Wed 24 Jun between 09:00–11:00 CET. Would Redwood be able to share a short MAP ahead of that call?

Best,

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear answers and the matrix. Quick technical follow-up and what Redwood can provide out of the box:

- Region pinning: We support tenant-level region pinning. For hosted EU pinning we provision capacity in the customer-selected EU region (Frankfurt or Amsterdam). When "hard pin" is selected, no production traffic or persistent prompt cache leaves EU by default.

- DR / backups: We can do same-region point-in-time backups by default. Geo-replication is available as an opt-in DR configuration; if you opt in, we can encrypt DR copies using a customer-managed KMS (we support AWS KMS + external key import for Dedicated/Private). Access controls for DR restores include role-based approval and an auditable restore workflow.

- Tokenization & logging: Recommended pattern — tokenization at ingress (your side or via a tokenization proxy) + zero-PII storage in logs. For debugging we provide hashed fingerprints and a gated debug endpoint for authorized engineers; access is audited.

- Retention defaults: Hosted default is 90 days for logs and 30 days for conversational inputs. These are configurable on dedicated deployments; per-account policies can be applied in the console.

- RTO/RPO: We can meet RPO <= 4 hours with async replication; RTO depends on whether you want fully automated failover (faster) or manual DR restores (we can hit 2 hours with pre-warmed standby for Dedicated but that is a higher cost tier).

Attached is a short proposal spreadsheet (redwood-residency-proposal-20260620.xlsx) that maps options -> cost delta -> operational notes. Also linking our residency docs and SOC 2 portal: https://docs.redwood.com/residency#region-pinning and https://security.redwood.com/soc2 (internal: HUBSPOT ORCH-4472).
